facts.value: There are a total of 4 different Business English courses (A-B-C-D) as part of the elective module courses in Business English. All courses are offered concurrently each semester.
All elective module courses have the same level of difficulty (target level C1.1 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages).

The successful completion of a qualifying test at CEFR level B2.2, which takes place at the beginning of each semester, is required if no Bachelor elective module course in Business English has been successfully completed.

Students who have the Cambridge Certificate C1, a score of 100 points or more in the TOEFL test, or a score of at least 7.5 in the IELTS test do not need to take the qualifying test but must upload proof in PDF format.
There is a two-stage application procedure with different deadlines. You must participate in both stages and pass the online qualifying test.
Enrollment period: September 21, 2026 – October 5, 2026 via QIS.
Exam registration and cancellation deadline: October 8, 2026 – October 21, 2026 via QIS.
Elective Module Course A: Current Global Economic Affairs
Monetary and financial policy, energy policy, global trade, migration and labor markets.
Joanne Glen, Guojun Wong, Barry Hawthorne.
Group 1: Monday, 2 PM – 4 PM, starts October 12, 2026; Group 2: Tuesday, 12 PM – 2 PM, starts October 13, 2026; Group 3: Thursday, 10 AM – 12 PM, starts October 15, 2026.
Elective Module Course B: Marketing
Marketing mix, behavioral economics and consumer behavior, digital marketing, gender, ethnicity and marketing, artificial intelligence, sustainability and ethical marketing, political marketing.
Caroline Pung.
Wednesday, 2 PM – 4 PM, starts October 14, 2026.
Elective Module Course C: The Entrepreneur
The entrepreneur and entrepreneurship, market research and feasibility analysis, strategy and pricing, marketing and branding, financial forecasting and financing.
Barry Hawthorne.
Tuesday, 10 AM – 12 PM, starts October 13, 2026.
Elective Module Course D: Banking & Financial Topics

Alternative finance: crowdfunding, shadow banking, complementary currencies; fintech: cryptocurrencies, cashless societies, fintech startups; ethical/social banking: Islamic banking, microfinance; current interest topics: stock market crisis, zombie companies, trade wars.
Caroline Pung.
Tuesday, 4 PM – 6 PM, starts October 13, 2026.
All participants receive 6 credit points for successfully completing a Business English elective module course: English for Economists.
An internal C1.1 certificate is issued for the successfully completed course.
